To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exaggerated cardiovascular responses during exercise are due to augmented central command and exercise pressor response in type II diabetic (T2DM) rats.

exaggerated pressor and sympathetic activity in response to stimulation of the putative central command site, the mesencephallic locomotor region (MRL), and activation of the exercise pressor response, evoked by electrical muscle stimulation, are observed in rats with type 2 (T2) diabetes.
the exaggerated cardiovascular responses to exercise in type 2 diabetes are generated by exaggerated responses of central command and the exercise press reflex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that contribute to the exaggerated cardiovascular responses during exercise observed in patients with T2DM.
the role of central and peripheral neural mechanisms in the regulation of the circulatory system during exercise in TDM.
the role of the central command and the exercise presser reflex in the development of the exaggerated cardiovascular responses to exercise in T2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exaggerated cardiovascular responses to exercise in T2MD are generated by the potentiation of both central command and exercise pressor responses.
the exaggerated pressor responses to exercise in T2D are due to augmented CC and EPR function.
the exaggerated cardiovascular responses to exercise in T2D is due to the augmentation of the central and peripheral components of the neural pathways involved in cardiovascular control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exaggerated pressor and sympathetic response to MLR stimulation as well as EER in type II diabetic animals may be due to a greater activation of CC and EPR pathways.
in the T2DM rat, the pressor response to MLR stimulation is augmented and that this augmentation is due to increased RSNA and increased sympathetic vasomotor tone.
the exaggerated pressor and sympathetic reflexes to exercise in type 2 diabetes are mediated by both augmented central command and exercise pressor mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exaggerated pressor response to exercise in T2D is not due to a single mechanism but rather the result of multiple mechanisms including augmented central command and the exercise presser reflex.
there is a significant increase in the pressor and sympathetic reflex response to both the exercise pressor and central command in type 2 diabetes.
the exaggerated cardiovascular responses to exercise in T2 diabetes may be caused by augmented central command and the exercise presso-reflex.
